routes.label: Assign professors to gaps between students

question: Nine chairs in a row are to be occupied by six students and Professors Alpha, Beta and Gamma. These three professors arrive before the six students and decide to choose their chairs so that each professor will be between two students. In how many ways can Professors Alpha, Beta and Gamma choose their chairs?
solution:
Each professor must have a student in the neighboring chair on each side. Thus no professor can occupy an end chair, and no two professors can sit next to each other.

Imagine starting with six student placeholders in a row. There are five internal gaps between consecutive placeholders. A professor may be inserted into any of these gaps, but at most one professor may go into a gap; otherwise two professors would be adjacent.

Alpha has five choices of gap. After Alpha chooses, Beta has four remaining choices, and Gamma then has three. By the multiplication principle, this gives
\[
5\cdot4\cdot3=60.
\]
To verify that this counts chair choices exactly once, insert the professors into their chosen gaps and number the resulting nine positions from left to right. This determines each professor's chair. Conversely, removing the professors from any valid seating pattern leaves six student placeholders and uniquely recovers each professor's gap. Thus every valid chair choice is included once.

The identities of the students do not create additional choices because the question asks only for the professors' chairs. The answer is \(\boxed{60}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
